1	composition:
2	  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
3	
4	# Normalize the telephone (strip non-digits, require exactly 10) first: it is the sole
5	# @RequestBody binding and must run before the DTO's digits-only pattern check would reject
6	# the raw input. It publishes the normalized body for the validate step.
7	normalize:
8	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
9	  next: normalizeEmail
10	
11	# Normalize the optional email (validate its format when present, then lower-case it) on the
12	# already-bound body, before validation and any persistence.
13	normalizeEmail:
14	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
15	  next: normalizeAddress
16	
17	# Normalize the address (trim/collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand abbreviations) on the
18	# already-bound body, before validation. Running before validate means an address blank once
19	# normalized is rejected as a missing required field, and every later address comparison
20	# (duplicate household, shared household id) sees the normalized form.
21	normalizeAddress:
22	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
23	  next: validate
24	
25	# Validate so a missing/blank required field is a 400 listing those fields, before any
26	# entity is built or persisted.
27	validate:
28	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
29	  next: validatePostcode
30	
31	# Validate the optional postcode when present: it must be valid for the city's region per the
32	# fixed ranges, else a 400. A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode; an absent
33	# postcode is skipped. Runs after field validation (which enforces the 4-digit format) and
34	# before any entity is built or persisted.
35	validatePostcode:
36	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerPostcode
37	  next: validateRegistrationDate
38	
39	# Reject a supplied registrationDate later than the server's current date with a 400, before
40	# any entity is built or persisted. An absent date is left to default downstream. Runs after
41	# the other field validations and before the date is resolved (weekend-adjusted).
42	validateRegistrationDate:
43	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerRegistrationDate
44	  next: unique
45	
46	# Reject a request whose derived identityKey (normalized telephone + email + household id)
47	# exactly matches an existing owner's with a 409, before any entity is built or persisted.
48	# This one key subsumes the former separate telephone, email and household checks: only a
49	# whole-key match is a duplicate, so household members with different telephones are allowed.
50	# Reads the same transaction as the writes.
51	unique:
52	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueOwnerIdentity
53	  govern: [ transaction ]
54	  next: cityCapacity
55	
56	# Reject the request with a 409 when its city already holds the maximum number of owners,
57	# before any entity is built or persisted. Reads the count in the same transaction as the
58	# writes so the per-city cap is enforced consistently.
59	cityCapacity:
60	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityHasCapacity
61	  govern: [ transaction ]
62	  next: resolveRegistrationDate
63	
64	# Resolve the effective registration date (supplied date, else the server's current date)
65	# and roll a weekend forward to the next Monday, before the daily-capacity check counts
66	# against it and before the owner is built. Publishes the adjusted date for both.
67	resolveRegistrationDate:
68	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ResolveOwnerRegistrationDate
69	  next: dailyCapacity
70	
71	# Reject the request with a 429 once the resolved business day (by adjusted registrationDate)
72	# already holds the maximum number of owner registrations, before any entity is built or
73	# persisted. Reads the count in the same transaction as the writes so the per-day limit is
74	# enforced consistently.
75	dailyCapacity:
76	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyOwnerCapacity
77	  govern: [ transaction ]
78	  next: build
79	
80	build:
81	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
82	  govern: [ transaction ]
83	  next: assignHousehold
84	assignHousehold:
85	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHousehold
86	  govern: [ transaction ]
87	  next: assignHouseholdSize
88	
89	# Record the size of this owner's household once the create completes (existing members
90	# sharing its household id plus the owner itself). Runs after the household id is assigned and
91	# backfilled, before the new owner is persisted, so the count reflects the state after the
92	# create without counting the owner twice.
93	assignHouseholdSize:
94	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHouseholdSize
95	  govern: [ transaction ]
96	  next: assignNamesakeCount
97	
98	# Record how many existing owners already shared this owner's firstName and lastName
99	# (case-insensitively) before this create. Reads the count in the same transaction as the
100	# write, before the new owner is persisted so it is not counted against itself.
101	assignNamesakeCount:
102	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerNamesakeCount
103	  govern: [ transaction ]
104	  next: assignMembershipLevel
105	
106	# Assign the numeric membership level from the built owner's email and namesake count: start at
107	# 1, +1 for an email, +1 when namesakeCount is 0, capped at 3. Runs after the namesake count is
108	# recorded and before the owner is persisted, so the level and the audit line reflect the final
109	# values.
110	assignMembershipLevel:
111	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerMembershipLevel
112	  govern: [ transaction ]
113	  next: assignBulkSignupWarning
114	
115	# Flag the built owner when more than 80 owners were already created for its resolved
116	# registration day. Reads the count in the same transaction as the write, before the new
117	# owner is persisted so it is not counted against itself.
118	assignBulkSignupWarning:
119	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerBulkSignupWarning
120	  govern: [ transaction ]
121	  next: applyRegistrationDate

123	# Stamp the resolved (weekend-adjusted) registration date onto the built owner before it is
124	# persisted, so it and every value derived from it use the adjusted business day.
125	applyRegistrationDate:
126	  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ApplyOwnerRegistrationDate
127	  govern: [ transaction ]
128	  next: assignCustomerCode

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner, stored in E.164 form.
          type: string
          minLength: 9
          maxLength: 16
          pattern: '^\+[0-9]{8,15}$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; when present it must be valid for the
            owner's city, i.e. within the inclusive range of the city's region (NSW 2000-2099,
            VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit
            postcode. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional on create; when omitted the server's current date is used.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-18'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The owner's date of birth, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional; when supplied it
            is stored and returned, and the owner's 'ageBand' is derived from it against the
            registrationDate.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, permits creating this owner even though another owner shares the same
            lastName and address (i.e. they live in the same household). Write-only; not stored
            or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The REGION segment of the owner's customerCode: the canonical region the code was
                built from (derived from the postcode range first, falling back to the fixed
                city-to-region table Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD, else 'UNKNOWN').
              type: string

## Change: soft-duplicate detection on owner creation

When a new owner isn't a hard identity duplicate but shares an existing owner's `lastName` and `postcode` with a *different* telephone, it's still created and now reports `possibleDuplicate: true` with `possibleDuplicateOf` set to the matched owner's id; otherwise `possibleDuplicate: false`.

I followed the existing "assign step" pattern used for the other derived owner fields (namesake count, membership level, bulk-signup warning), keeping each piece in its own small unit:

A shared postcode is required to match.

2. **Pipeline wiring** — `owners.POST.yml`: inserted the `assignPossibleDuplicate` step (under `transaction` governance) between `assignBulkSignupWarning` and `applyRegistrationDate`. Hard duplicates are still rejected upstream by `EnsureUniqueOwnerIdentity`, so this only ever flags genuine soft matches.

3. **Entity** — `Owner.java`: added `possibleDuplicate` (Boolean) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (Integer) columns with accessors.

4. **Schema** — added `possible_duplicate` / `possible_duplicate_of` columns to all four `schema.sql` files (hsqldb/h2/postgres/mysql); tests run on hsqldb with `ddl-auto=none`, so the DDL had to be explicit.

5. **API contract** — `openapi.yml`: added the two read-only properties to the `Owner` schema, which regenerates `OwnerDto`; MapStruct auto-maps the same-named entity fields, so the `GET /api/owners/{id}` response carries them with no mapper change needed.

The `AcceptanceTest.coreFlagsPossibleDuplicate` test and the full suite are green.
